M1.reason: Outline matches the brief in all ten views: an upright, slightly stooped older man in a knee-length white coat with a flared hem, light trousers and brown shoes. The walk and run poses in the side and angle views keep the same outline, and nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Height is 68 units, exactly the brief's ~68. The brief gives no width or depth, so only height is held here (33.3 wide, 21.7 deep, both unspecified by the brief).

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: glasses (black frames on both sides, visible in front, left, right and back-quarter views), bald crown with grey hair above the ears, blue shirt collar, red tie with a dark pattern (painted on the shirt, and it reads at this size in the front view), white lapelled coat over the shirt, a belt, light trousers, and two brown shoes. Nothing asked for is missing or the wrong count. The lens and collar shapes are not specified by the brief, so they are not charged.

M4.reason: Each region matches the brief's colours: white lab coat, blue shirt, red-and-dark tie, light trousers, grey hair, skin, brown shoes, dark glasses frames. Shown consistently across all ten views and the run frames.

M5.reason: Face detail (eyes, nose, glasses), coat folds and lapels, the shirt collar and the tie pattern are there, in their places, at a sharpness close to Half-Life's own figures in the line-up. The brief asks for no markings, so nothing is charged for their absence.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, which is measured apart. In three readings with the asset at D, B and C, the judges picked C, A and A: never the asset, so it passed for one of the game's three times out of three.

M7.reason: The front is the front: the face and glasses turn toward the front view and the figure stands upright. In the front and back views the feet sit on the same floor line, so it stands on its origin as Half-Life's figures do.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks pass with no errors. 740 triangles is within twice the median of Half-Life's own people (504 gives a bound of 1,008) and under the 1,640 most that Valve spends on one. No gap or floating part shows in the side, angle or run views. The dark patches in the underside view look like the shoe soles, which a player seldom sees from below and which are not a gap in the outline.

C1.reason: In the 18-frame run, the arms swing in step with the legs, the coat tails trail and the feet strike the floor line in turn. Every part stays on the body and moves as a run does, with nothing sinking into the floor or floating.
